response.query: How can we test and rule out reverse causality between revenue and satisfaction using timing, dynamic-panel estimators, placebo tests, and pre-specified lag structures?
response.answer: To test reverse causality, use dynamic-panel estimators with pre-specified lag structures, conduct placebo tests, and ensure timing aligns revenue changes before satisfaction changes.

results.title: Research Seminars | Economics - Union College
results.content: * October 2, 2025: Minsik Choi (Ewha Womans) ~ The Price of a Name: Rent-seeking, Subway Station Renaming, and Neighborhood Housing Prices. Peer Health Shocks and Labor Supply. * April 2, 2026: Dolores Garrido (Union) ~ Job Security and Housing Wealth Risk: Evidence from U.S. Counties. Abstract: Existing literature has studied the role that the gender composition of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) plays in meeting dynamics and resulting policy decisions; however, an important topic that has received little attention is whether and how the gender composition of the FOMC affects meeting participants’ behavior at various levels of the career ladder. Importantly, we show that the presence of more women on the FOMC is associated with changing behavior of female FRS staff members. We also establish that some meeting behaviors are associated with career progression, including ones that are affected by the presence of more women on the FOMC.
